COURSE TITLE    ADMINISTRATIVE LAW
COURSE CODE     10FL1505
COURSE CREDITS  4

Objective:
 1  To understand the meaning, scope, and nature of administrative law.
 2  To understand the Rule of Law, Rule against Bias, and Principles of Natural Justice.
 3  To make the students learn the classification of administrative functions. i.e. quasi-judicial,
      legislative, and purely administrative functions and the controls over them.
 4  To provide students with knowledge and appreciation of the differences between
     constitutional law administrative law and judicial process.
 5  To provide students with an awareness of principles underpinning the legal doctrine of the
    emerging trend in administrative law.


Course Outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able to:
 1  To define the meaning and scope of administrative law and delegated legislation.
 2  To state the principles of natural justice.
 3  To explain administrative adjudication.
 4  To discuss administrative discretion and remedies.
 5  To interpret the liability of the administration.
 6  To compare administrative process and judicial review.

Objective:
 1  Develop an understanding of the important role of evidence in law and legal proceedings.
 2  Gain insight into the criteria determining the admissibility of different types of evidence.

     admissibility status.

     admissibility.

    showcasing a nuanced understanding of evidence types.
 4   Critically evaluate the validity and limitations of dying declarations, demonstrating
     analytical skills in assessing evidence.
 5  Assess the significance and relevance of witness examination in court proceedings,
     highlighting the practical application of evidence evaluation.
